content_metadata.description: An educational video explaining the process of sexual reproduction in plants, including the roles of flowers, pollination, and fertilization.

qAndA.question: What are the four parts of a typical angiosperm flower?

qAndA.answer: Essential whorls (androecium and gynoecium) produce gametes during reproduction. Non-essential whorls (calyx and corolla) are protective and do not participate in reproduction.
qAndA.question: What is the difference between essential and non-essential whorls?

qAndA.answer: A process unique to angiosperms where one male gamete fuses with the egg cell to form a zygote, while the other male gamete fuses with the polar nuclei to form the endosperm.
qAndA.question: What is double fertilization?

qAndA.answer: Ovules develop into seeds, and the ovary develops into a fruit.
qAndA.question: What do the ovules and ovary develop into after fertilization?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Sexual reproduction in plants.
In all higher plants, flower is a reproductive organ and angiospermic flower typically bears
four parts or voles, namely, calyx, carola, androsium and gynosium.
Out of these, calyx and carola are protective in function and do not participate in the process.
Hence, they are called non-essential voles.
Andresium and gynesium produce gametes during reproduction.
Therefore, they are called essential voles.
When all these four parts are present, the flower is said to be complete and bisexual.
Calyx is made up of sepals and carola has petals.
Andresium has stamens and a single member of gynosium is called a carpal or pistil.
Each stamens has anthors.
Poling greens are produced inside anthors by meiosis.
Each carpal has ovary at the base, which has one or many ovules.
The ovules excel and two polar nuclei are produced by meiosis.
Poling greens are transferred from one another to stigma during pollination.
Poling greens germinate on stigma to produce poland tube.
This poland tube carries two male gametes.
Poland tube reaches the embryo sac.
One male gamete fuses with the excel to form zygote.
The second male gamete fuses with the polar nuclei to form the endosperm.
As both nuclei are used and the event of fertilization occurs twice, this is called a double
fertilization.
After fertilization, zygote develops into embryo, ovules develop into seeds and ovary into
fruit.
